issues.detail: The Greek 'οι δε αποκριθεντες' refers to the people who had already responded/answered (the respondents). The Vietnamese translation 'Họ' (They) is too general and loses the specific context of those who were responding in the legal proceeding.

The Greek 'ενοχος θανατου εστιν' means 'he is guilty of death' (or 'guilty of a death penalty'). The Vietnamese 'Nó đáng chết' (It/He deserves to die) shifts the focus from 'guilt' to 'deserving,' which slightly alters the legal status described in the Greek.
